claims.text: Conventionally processed Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 forms multiple crystalline phases and exhibits a complex crystallization sequence.
The crystalline phases formed during conventional processing are primary non-eutectic phases.
Ultra-rapid melt-spinning followed by sub-crystallization reheating will suppress primary crystallization in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Ultra-rapid melt-spinning at cooling rates of 10^5–10^6 K/s produces an amorphous Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 structure.
Reheating below approximately 1206 K will avoid triggering extensive crystallization.
Approximately 1206 K is the relevant first major crystallization boundary for the proposed reheating treatment.
The reported eutectic crystallization temperature is approximately 1206 K during slow cooling and shifts to 960 K under accelerated cooling.
Ultra-rapid cooling suppresses nucleation and growth by minimizing the time available for primary-phase formation.
Sub-crystallization reheating permits only limited atomic mobility and therefore prevents extensive crystallization.
The proposed reheating treatment will relieve stresses and stabilize the amorphous structure.
Phosphorus enhances the glass-forming ability of Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 during rapid cooling.
The combined treatment will produce a higher amorphous fraction than slow cooling at about 52 K/s or accelerated cooling at about 3018 K/s.
The combined treatment will increase thermal stability and shift the crystallization onset to a higher temperature relative to standard rapid cooling without reheating.
The combined treatment will delay crystallization during subsequent thermal exposure.
Slow cooling at approximately 52 K/s produces a complex crystalline microstructure.
Accelerated cooling after a short electric-arc pulse at approximately 3018 K/s reduces the phase count but does not produce the fully amorphous structure obtained by melt-spinning.
The exact safe reheating-temperature bounds and the magnitude of the increase in amorphous retention are not known.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis treats approximately 1206 K as a generally safe reheating ceiling or first crystallization onset, even though the same cited cooling-rate behavior places eutectic crystallization as low as 960 K under accelerated cooling. A boundary merely below 1206 K therefore does not necessarily remain below crystallization.
